LVMH shares fall after Iran war hits first-quarter sales
STORY: Shares in French luxury goods group LVMH fell as much as 3% on Tuesday after first-quarter sales were hit.It's as the war in Iran hit spending by Middle Eastern shoppers, further delaying a long-awaited recovery for the luxury sector leader.LVMH owns 75 brands including Louis Vuitton, Dior, and Tiffany & Co.It said on Monday the conflict shaved at least 1 percentage point off global sales.The hit reflected weaker spending in Gulf shopping hubs like Dubai.And fewer Middle Eastern shoppers travelling to Europe.LVMH shares are down just over a quarter since the start of the year as hopes for a rebound in luxury demand have faded.Disruption and inflation caused by the war has caused a new obstacle to growth.One financial adviser told Reuters higher energy prices and mortgage rates are likely to curb demand from middle-class, or so-called "aspirational", luxury consumers.LVMH said mall traffic in the Middle East, which accounts for about 6% of group turnover, initially dropped by between 30% and 70%.Investors will watch for the war's impact on other luxury brands when Gucci owner Kering reports after the market close on Tuesday.Hermes also gives its first-quarter results Wednesday morning.
